AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-20

Generated: 2026-11-20 02:14 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report — AI CLI Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-20 | Scope: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tooling landscape on 2026-11-20 shows a maturing market where agent orchestration, MCP interoperability, and cross-surface continuity have replaced raw model access as the primary competitive battleground. Release cadence remains high (Codex, Gemini CLI, and Copilot CLI all shipped within 24h), but the dominant activity is reliability engineering: subagent lifecycle management, prompt-cache correctness, context-window economics, and terminal state hygiene. A notable structural pattern is the convergence of desktop, TUI, IDE, and web surfaces around a shared agent runtime — and the attendant bugs when that shared state leaks across surfaces. Safety and trust infrastructure (Claude Code's fork-PR hardening, Qwen Code's AUTO-mode trust bypass, Codex's approval-authority validation) is emerging as a first-class engineering concern rather than a compliance afterthought.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (24h window) PRs (24h window) Discussions Release Status
Claude Code ~30+ active (≈25 are one reporter's cyber-filter cluster) 1 updated (1 open) N/A (not provided) v2.1.329 shipped
OpenAI Codex 10+ hot issues tracked 10 updated (9 internal refactors + 1 security) ✅ Multiple (Ideas, Q&A, Show & Tell) rust-v0.171.0 stable; v0.172.0-alpha.2; v0.171.0-alpha.13.1
Gemini CLI 10 hot issues tracked 10 updated (6 closed, 4 open) N/A (not provided) v0.70.0 stable; v0.71.0-preview.0; nightly
GitHub Copilot CLI 10 hot issues tracked 1 updated (closed) N/A (not provided) v1.0.115-1 + v1.0.115-0
OpenCode 10 hot issues tracked 10 updated (multiple) N/A (not provided) No release
Pi 10 hot issues tracked 10 updated (8 closed, 2 open) ✅ Multiple (Show & Tell, Ideas) No release
Qwen Code 10 hot issues tracked 10 updated N/A (not provided) No release

Notes:

  • Counts reflect only items updated in the last 24h as reported in source digests; absolute repository totals are not comparable.
  • N/A for Discussions indicates the digest source did not provide Discussion data — not that the channel is inactive. Codex and Pi are the only tools with confirmed Discussion activity in this window.
  • Claude Code's issue count is inflated by a single reporter (sworrl) filing ~25 cyber-safeguard false positives; the distinct signal count is closer to 5–6 issues.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Several requirements recur independently across tool communities, indicating ecosystem-level rather than tool-specific demand:

3.1 Subagent maturity & lifecycle control

  • Gemini CLI — the overwhelming theme: async/background execution (#17754), resumability (#17758), per-agent configurability (#17760), shared memory/parallel collaboration (#18287).
  • OpenCode — subagent hallucination when idle (#63785), background-service reliability (#64869).
  • Codex — subagent transcripts in TUI (#61352), orchestration with model routing (#62394).
  • Claude Code — scheduled tasks//loop visibility in v2.1.329.

Common need: agents that run durably, in parallel, and observably — with the ability to resume, isolate, and inspect them.

3.2 MCP reliability & trust boundaries

  • Copilot CLI — the #1 pain point: OAuth silent failures, missing token exchange, forced re-auth despite valid refresh tokens (#4017, #4203, #5350, #5510).
  • Qwen Code — AUTO-mode MCP trust bypass (#17854, security), "still connecting" indistinguishable from "failed" (#17832), elicitation capability (#17358).
  • Codex — full Apps/MCP catalog sent per request causing context overflow (#61679); mcpServerStatus/list failures (#62631).
  • OpenCode — mid-conversation tool changes requiring re-declaration (#64381).

Common need: MCP as a first-class, trustable, context-efficient integration surface — not a bolted-on tool loader.

3.3 Context-window economics & compaction correctness

  • Copilot CLI — PDF token overcounting (~20×, #5517), silent 128K fallback (#4310).
  • Codex — Apps catalog inflation → auto-compaction loops (#61679).
  • Qwen Code — double-counted pending tool result aborting turns (#15486), compaction truncating user prompts (#17894).
  • Pi — GPT-6.2 cache-reuse regression (#12273), thinking-level changes breaking cache (#12269).
  • Gemini CLI — "Tactful Extraction" grep-first read hierarchy (#19561); baseline ~36.6k tokens/turn.

Common need: deterministic, transparent token accounting and cache-preserving session mutations.

3.4 Terminal/TUI lifecycle hygiene

  • Pi — the single most concentrated bug cluster: SIGTSTP handling, mouse-tracking leaks, Kitty keyboard protocol not restored on exit (#12133, #12272, #12283, #12336, #12339).
  • Copilot CLI — timeline jumps, non-collapsing reasoning blocks, diff panels pushing context off-screen (#5533, #5531).
  • Claude Code — Windows claude.exe session-process accumulation (#96299).

Common need: clean suspend/resume/exit semantics and review-friendly TUI state.

3.5 Workspace/project scoping

  • Codex — per-workspace chat history (#25319, 👍139 — highest-engagement issue in this report), project-first sidebar.
  • OpenCode — per-project credential activation (#51152) to stop cross-project re-billing.
  • Gemini CLI — per-workspace policy scoping (#18397).

Common need: isolation boundaries so one project's context, credentials, and billing don't bleed into another.

3.6 Cross-surface continuity

  • Codex — ChatGPT mobile ↔ Codex desktop bidirectional handoff (#32519).
  • Claude Code — Desktop + non-interactive host parity for hook warnings.
  • Gemini CLI — ACP session lifecycle (#30368) for editor integration.

4. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension Claude Code OpenAI Codex Gemini CLI Copilot CLI OpenCode Pi Qwen Code
Primary focus Enterprise hooks/automation + safety Model catalog + TUI workspace Subagent framework + native bash MCP auth + IDE/ACP integration Provider flexibility + plugin parity Embedded agent runtime + durable storage Managed channels + CI reliability
Target user Enterprise/CI, security-conscious teams Broad IDE + desktop developer Power users of agentic workflows GitHub-centric devs, Zed/ACP users Multi-provider tinkerers, plugin authors Embedders, "always-on agent" builders Managed-agent / enterprise channel operators
Technical approach Hook provenance, trust dialogs, fork-PR gating Rust core, catalog-driven routing, Guardian classifier Native bash affinity, zero-dep sandboxing proposal ACP-first, MCP OAuth state machine Background shared server, session_part row storage pi-durable, package namespacing, WebDriver quota ideas Daemon recovery inbox, channel adapters
Distinctive asset Managed-settings hook trust model GPT-6.2 Sol/Astra as default + TUI doc previews Gemini 3 POSIX-tool affinity Extension bootstrap + MCP scopes Claude account rotation Terminal lifecycle rigor MCP elicitation + skill-declared MCP deps
Biggest self-inflicted risk Over-broad cyber filter halting sessions Windows desktop instability Generalist agent hangs (P1) MCP OAuth opacity Provider/model identity churn Windows second-class treatment Chronically red main CI

Key differentiators:

  • Claude Code is the only tool where safety infrastructure itself is the dominant community signal — and where that infrastructure is visibly over-triggering.
  • Codex is the only tool with a model catalog as a shipped feature (Sol default, Astra added) — competing on model access, not just harness.
  • Gemini CLI has the most coherent subagent roadmap (epics #17754/#17758/#17760/#18287 cross-referenced).
  • Copilot CLI is the most MCP-auth-fragile and the most ACP-invested (Zed integration).
  • Pi differentiates on durable, embeddable runtime (pi-durable, pi.namespace, Telegram-backed always-on agent in #12331).
  • Qwen Code is uniquely channel-oriented (DingTalk/WeCom/GitHub managed adapters) — an enterprise-messaging-first posture.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

5.1 Momentum ranking (activity intensity, 24h window)

Tier Tools Evidence
Highest OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode 10+ PRs updated, multiple hot issues with high 👍/comment counts, active Discussions (Codex, Pi)
High Claude Code, Qwen Code Very high issue volume (Claude: ~30; Qwen: 484-comment CI issue) but lower PR throughput in window
Moderate GitHub Copilot CLI Only 1 PR updated in 24h; issue engagement is real but PR velocity is thin

5.2 Maturity signals

  • Most mature harness engineering: OpenAI Codex — 10 PRs in 24h, mostly internal refactors (memory release, executor cache reuse, backpressure, ID centralization), plus a security fix (#30963). This is the profile of a system being hardened, not rescued.
  • Most mature community engagement: Codex (Discussions with 150+ tool indexes, plugin manifests) and Pi (Show & Tell with 5,216-line real deployments).
  • Fastest iteration: Gemini CLI — stable + preview + nightly in one window, with /stats heatmap shipped.
  • Most fragile CI: Qwen Code — Managed Agent gate chronically red since ≥2026-11-11 (#17851), making required-check gating effectively meaningless; 484-comment bot-filed issue (#14724) signals noise fatigue.
  • Most fragile user trust: Claude Code — a single reporter's ~25 false positives indicate a systemic filter calibration problem, not isolated reports.
  • Most concentrated UX debt: Pi — a dozen PRs in 24h all addressing terminal lifecycle; high fix velocity but reveals accumulated debt.

5.3 Community health caveats

  • Copilot CLI's low PR count (1) with high issue engagement may indicate a bottleneck in maintainer review or a shift of development to a private/upstream repo.
  • Claude Code's issue tracker is currently distorted by the cyber-filter cluster; true community signal is thinner than raw counts suggest.
  • OpenCode's 161-comment clipboard issue (#4283, closed) and 135 👍 show a passionate user base willing to doggedly reproduce bugs — a healthy sign.

6. Trend Signals

6.1 Industry-level trends visible in community feedback

  1. Safety filters are becoming a developer-experience liability. Claude Code's cyber-filter false-positive cluster (firmware flashing, Go builds, TLS setup, defensive hardening) is the clearest signal yet that lexical/topic-based safety classifiers over-trigger on legitimate engineering work. Expect demand for intent-aware, domain-scoped safeguards and per-project allowlists.

  2. MCP is the new "integration tax." Across Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Codex, and OpenCode, MCP lifecycle — OAuth, trust, catalog inflation, elicitation — is the single most cross-cutting pain point. Tools that solve MCP reliability (not just MCP support) will win enterprise adoption.

  3. Prompt-cache correctness is now a cost feature. Pi's GPT-6.2 cache-reuse regression (#12273), OpenCode's plan-limit drain (#61072), and Codex's context overflow all point to the same truth: token accounting bugs are now billing bugs. Cache-preserving session mutations (#12269) are a genuine differentiator.

  4. Subagents are the next platform primitive. Gemini CLI's epic cluster, Codex's subagent transcripts, and OpenCode's subagent hallucination issue all indicate the industry is moving from single-agent chat to orchestrated multi-agent runtimes — and the tooling to observe, resume, and isolate them is immature.

  5. Terminal/TUI state hygiene is a trust proxy. Pi's concentrated terminal-lifecycle fixes and Copilot CLI's TUI friction show that users judge tool quality by whether their shell is intact after exit. This is unglamorous but high-leverage.

  6. Cross-surface continuity is the emerging expectation. Codex's mobile↔desktop handoff request (#32519) and Gemini CLI's ACP work signal that developers expect the same agent context across surfaces — a hard architectural problem that will separate leaders from laggards.

  7. Windows remains a second-class citizen across the board. Codex (project disappearance, WSL disk exhaustion), Claude Code (process leaks, silent notifications), Pi (99-comment Windows thread, re-render saturation), Gemini CLI (PowerShell freezes, ~\ paths), Copilot CLI (vim backspace, long-path clones) — every tool has Windows-specific debt. Enterprise Windows adoption will be gated by this.

  8. CI reliability is a community-trust issue, not just an ops issue. Qwen Code's chronically red main and 484-comment bot issue show that unstable required checks erode contributor confidence and generate noise that masks real bugs.

6.2 Reference value for developers & decision-makers

  • If you need model-access breadth: Codex (Sol/Astra catalog) leads; watch for catalog-driven routing (#61844).
  • If you need enterprise MCP reliability: None are fully there yet; Copilot CLI is most exposed, Qwen Code is most actively hardening trust boundaries.
  • If you need durable/embeddable agents: Pi (pi-durable, pi.namespace) and OpenCode (background server) are the most architecturally ambitious.
  • If you need safety/audit trails: Claude Code's hook-trust model is the most developed — but budget for filter calibration.
  • If you need channel/enterprise-messaging integration: Qwen Code (DingTalk/WeCom/GitHub) is the outlier leader.
  • If you value CI hygiene: Qwen Code is the cautionary tale; Codex's refactor-heavy PR flow is the model to emulate.

Report compiled from seven 2026-11-20 community digests. Counts reflect only items updated in the 24h window and are not directly comparable across repositories. Where source data was absent (Discussions for five tools), sections are marked N/A rather than inferred.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Data snapshot: 2026-11-20 · Source: github.com/anthropics/skills

1. Top Skills Ranking (by discussion & attention)

Note: The PR feed reports Comments: undefined for all entries, so ranking below is inferred from cross-referencing with linked Issues, author activity, and PR prominence.

# Skill / PR Functionality Discussion Highlights Status
1 mcp-builder fix — #1742 Patches MCP connection scripts for mcp>=2.0.0 API rename (streamablehttp_client → streamable_http_client) and header config Breaks real-world MCP integrations; fix linked to issue #1668. Active since Sept. OPEN
2 skill-creator trigger-eval fix — #1298 Isolates trigger evaluations, fixes Windows subprocess select() failures and runtime-failure misclassification Addresses the same false-negative trigger problem reported in Issues #556 and #1352 OPEN

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

Distilled from the highest-engagement Issues:

  • Trust & namespace security — Issue #492 (46 comments): community skills distributed under the anthropic/ namespace enable impersonation and trust-boundary abuse. This is by far the loudest concern.
  • Enterprise / org-wide skill distribution — Issue #228 (17 👍): users want shared skill libraries and direct share links instead of manual .skill file uploads.
  • Skill evaluation correctness — Issue #556 and #1352: run_eval.py produces 0% trigger rates, and parallel workers cross-match UUIDs — undermining skill QA.
  • Context economy — Issue #1487: the claude-api skill injects ~156k tokens in one call, exhausting the context window. Demand for leaner, lazy-loading skills.
  • Skill description quality — Issue #2064: frontmatter should say when to use a skill, not just what it does (triggerability).
  • Memory / reasoning scaffolding — Issue #1329 (compact-memory) and #1385 (Reasoning Quality Gate Pipeline): symbolic agent state compression and pre-task/adversarial/delivery quality gates.
  • Plugin duplication & packaging — Issue #189: document-skills and example-skills ship identical content, causing context bloat.

Emerging directions: workflow automation (spec→tasks), agent self-governance/quality gates, memory compression, Web3 auditing, and document/typography quality control.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills (active, unmerged)

PR Skill Why it may land soon

#1950 claude-api pause_turn guidance Updated 2026-11-10; aligns docs with Python SDK 1.1.0 auto-resumption
#2019 xlsx external-link resolution Updated 2026-11-03; closes issue #2013, well-scoped bug fix
#2108 README snapshot-status docs Updated 2026-11-03; low-risk documentation clarity

#1615 scnet-hpc HPC/Slurm domain skill; self-contained

Observation: The majority of pending PRs are bug fixes to existing official skills, not new skill submissions — a sign the ecosystem is maturing toward maintenance and hardening.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is for trust, correctness, and context-efficiency in the Skills pipeline itself — secure namespacing, reliable trigger/eval behavior, and lean token footprints — rather than for entirely new skill categories.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-20

1. Today's Highlights

A new patch release (v2.1.329) landed with hook-trust and scheduled-task visibility improvements, but the day's activity was dominated by a large batch of closed cybersecurity safeguard false-positive reports from a single reporter (sworrl) and several long-running Windows/desktop bugs. Notably, a fresh PR (#111198) proposes blocking @claude mentions on fork-originated pull requests — a meaningful security hardening step for the agent-triggered workflow.

2. Releases

v2.1.329 — small but useful trust/observability update:

  • Added a trust dialog warning that indicates where a folder's hooks are declared.
  • Added an in-conversation warning (Claude Desktop and other non-interactive hosts) when hooks in managed settings fail to load.
  • Added visibility into the current session's scheduled tasks, /loop wakeups, and the active goal.

These changes target transparency around hook execution and automated/scheduled agent behavior — a recurring theme in enterprise/CI usage.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #93482 — Cowork silent stale writes (Windows, data-loss) — device_commit_files reports success on overwrites, but on-disk content lags exactly one commit behind (fresh mtime, stale body). 28 comments, 2 👍. A genuine data-integrity bug in the cowork/device sync path; the most-discussed issue of the day. Link

  2. #96299 — Windows claude.exe session processes never terminated — Background processes accumulate over a workday, driving high RAM/disk usage. 13 comments, 4 👍. Persistent resource leak affecting the desktop app on Windows. Link

  3. #95593 — Desktop completion notifications silent (Windows + macOS) — Chat response notifications don't fire, while Code/Cowork notifications work correctly. 10 comments, 4 👍. Cross-platform desktop UX regression. Link

  4. #105868 — mcp__claude-in-chrome__file_upload missing from new chats — Tool intermittently absent; latest update: works only in automatic approval mode, with a ~3.8 MB payload concern noted. 7 comments, 4 👍. MCP tool-availability inconsistency in Claude-in-Chrome. Link

  5. #94159 — Safeguard false positive halting microcontroller firmware flashing — Opus 4.8 cyber filter blocked authorized hardware work; reproducible via Request ID. Link

  6. #94157 — Safeguard block on defensive code fix commits — Session-halted during routine defensive patching. Link

  7. #94142 — Safeguard flagged embedded Linux image compilation / power wake verification — 1 👍; representative of the embedded/firmware cluster of false positives. Link

  8. #94137 — Safeguards block Go build script review / cross-platform compilation — infra-devops domain, 1 👍; shows the filter triggering on ordinary build tooling. Link

  9. #94141 — Safeguard blocks key search in local backups during server hardening — defensive-hardening domain; a defensive-security task blocked by the safety filter. Link

  10. #94136 — Safeguard blocks updating test files/mock data to compliant terminology — offensive-pentest domain; even terminology cleanup was flagged. Link

Note on the cyber cluster: Roughly 25 of the top 30 issues by comment count today are [Bug][cyber] safeguard false-positive reports authored by sworrl — almost all CLOSED (many marked duplicate), tagged area:security/area:model/api:anthropic, with flagging model Opus 4.8 and severity session-halted. The cluster is significant as a signal: the cyber safety filter appears to be broadly over-triggering on legitimate embedded, defensive, and build/review work.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24h:

  1. #111198 — "Don't run @claude mentions on pull requests from forks" (OPEN, by mhegazy) — Proposes that an @claude mention on a fork-originated PR should not trigger the agent. This is a supply-chain/abuse-prevention measure: fork PRs are attacker-controllable, so auto-running an agent on them risks prompt-injection and secret-exposure vectors. Community reaction data (comments/reactions) is not yet available. Link

With only a single PR in the window, no further PRs can be meaningfully summarized without speculation.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in the source payload. This section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Inferred from the issue set (feature requests are limited; the dominant signal is bug-driven):

  • Hook/automation transparency — v2.1.329's trust-dialog and managed-settings hook warnings reflect ongoing demand for clearer provenance and failure reporting around hooks and scheduled tasks.
  • MCP tool reliability — #105868 highlights demand for consistent availability of MCP tools (e.g., Chrome file upload) across chat modes and hosts.
  • Desktop lifecycle management — #96299 and #95593 point to requests for proper process cleanup and consistent cross-platform notification behavior.
  • Safety-filter precision — the cyber cluster is effectively a large-scale request for a more precise, domain-aware safeguard that distinguishes authorized embedded/defensive work from genuinely malicious activity.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Over-broad cybersecurity safeguards (highest-volume pain point). Dozens of session-halting false positives on firmware flashing, Go builds, TLS setup, AD CS lookups, local DNS, backup key search, and documentation updates. The pattern suggests the filter keys on lexical/topic cues rather than intent, blocking legitimate defensive-hardening, infra-devops, and embedded work.
  • Windows desktop resource leaks. Session processes accumulating with no termination (#96299) and silent completion notifications (#95593) degrade the day-to-day desktop experience.
  • Silent data staleness. The one-commit-behind write behavior in Cowork (#93482) is especially dangerous because it reports success — eroding trust in the tool's commit semantics.
  • MCP tool inconsistency. Tools appearing/disappearing and behaving differently by approval mode (#105868) makes Chrome automation unreliable.

Prepared from github.com/anthropics/claude-code data for 2026-11-20. Issue/PR counts reflect only items updated in the last 24h; comment and reaction totals are as reported in the source.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-20

1. Today's Highlights

The rust-v0.171.0 stable release landed with two major changes: GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra added to model catalogs (Sol now the default), and the TUI workspace enabled by default with searchable document/image previews and subagent transcripts. Meanwhile, the issue tracker is dominated by Windows desktop regressions (disappearing projects, WSL disk exhaustion, Chrome control failures) and a notable context-window exhaustion bug where the Apps tool catalog is sent in full on every request, triggering auto-compaction loops.

2. Releases

rust-v0.171.0 (stable)

  • Model catalogs updated: Added GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra, with Sol as the default catalog selection (#62106).
  • TUI workspace on by default: Searchable document previews, image previews, and subagent transcripts now render alongside the main conversation (#61352, #61888, #61889, #61919).

rust-v0.172.0-alpha.2

  • Pre-release build; no detailed changelog provided.

rust-v0.171.0-alpha.13.1

  • Patch-level alpha; no detailed changelog provided.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #25319 — Scope Codex VS Code chats to the current workspace/project (61 comments, 👍139) The highest-engagement open issue. IDE Extension users want chat/thread history scoped per workspace instead of globally, avoiding cross-project context bleed. Massive 👍 count signals broad demand.

  2. #62212 — Desktop: unsupported audio tool output causes later text-only turns to return HTTP 400 (28 comments) A fresh, high-traffic bug: an audio tool response poisons subsequent text-only turns with HTTP 400 on GPT-6.2 Sol. Serious because it breaks sessions mid-workflow and appears reproducible.

  3. #25737 — CLI login forces SMS OTP on security-key-only (AAS) accounts (24 comments, 👍12) A long-running auth inconsistency: browser login honors Advanced Account Security (FIDO2/CTAP2), but codex login forces an SMS phone OTP step-up. Blocks hardware-key-only users from the CLI.

  4. #47041 — GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-6 Astra reject harmless prompts with invalid_prompt (16 comments) Model-behavior regression on Windows desktop where benign prompts are rejected. Persistent for two months; undermines trust in the new default models.

  5. #32519 — ChatGPT–Codex shared project context and bidirectional task handoff (12 comments) Feature request for seamless context flow between ChatGPT mobile (ideation) and Codex desktop (implementation). Reflects the growing "multi-surface workflow" expectation.

  6. #61294 — Windows: local Codex projects disappear after update while chats remain accessible (11 comments) Update-induced data-loss-style regression on Windows: projects vanish from the sidebar while threads survive. High user anxiety, zero 👍 but high severity.

  7. #38768 — Windows Remote Control: WebSocket times out (os error 10060) behind proxy/TUN (10 comments) Corporate-proxy and TUN users cannot establish Remote Control connections despite curl reaching the endpoint. Blocks enterprise adoption.

  8. #30417 — ChatGPT mobile incorrectly blocks Codex Cloud when Remote Control is disabled (10 comments, 👍6) Entitlement gating bug: mobile Codex surface is locked behind Remote Control even when Codex Cloud is enabled and works on web/Slack. Confusing UX.

  9. #61679 — Apps tool catalog sent in full every request → fresh session exceeds context window, auto-compaction loops (5 comments) Architecturally significant: full MCP/Apps catalog inflation on every request causes immediate context overflow. A real blocker for MCP-heavy users.

  10. #56601 — Allow CLI/TUI users to connect a computer to a dot without the desktop app (👍13) High-signal enhancement: CLI-first users want dot/computer pairing without the desktop app. Strong 👍 despite only 4 comments.

4. Key PR Progress

Most PRs this cycle are copyberry[bot]-authored internal refactors. The notable ones:

  1. #62644 — Pass inherited history visibility to the thread store Adds InheritedHistoryVisibility to CreateThreadParams; ModelContextOnly lets forks omit history from list_turns/list_items. Foundation for cleaner forked context.

  2. #62641 — Release persisted MCP tool results from active-turn memory Frees memory for completed MCP tool results when history can supply the payload — with truncation-preview safety checks. Directly relevant to the context/memory pressure in #61679.

  3. #62640 — Reuse executor Discovery V2 inventories across turns Stops discarding the discovery cache at turn start, avoiding redundant MCP inventory rebuilds.

  4. #62639 — Defer queue-only mail after a retained final answer Prevents spurious turn resampling when a final answer is already retained after a mailbox interrupt.

  5. #62636 — Reduce rollout scanning overhead when listing threads Uses buffered rollout reading and skips unrelated record parsing — a thread-list performance win.

  6. #62635 — Centralize request and prefix ID handling in ThreadContextIds Stable, thread-scoped, content-derived UUIDs for base instructions and Responses Lite tool definitions.

  7. #62627 — Retry Guardian model discovery in the background Prevents a failed catalog fetch from leaving a configured Guardian provider without a classifier, avoiding tool-dispatch delays.

  8. #62615 — Split in-memory execution policy rules into a separate crate Decouples config/protocol/prompt code from the Starlark parser — meaningful build and layering cleanup.

  9. #62609 — Apply backpressure to app-server request replay on thread resume Bounds outbound queue pressure when resuming threads with many pending requests.

  10. #30963 — Validate approval responses against pending authority (OPEN since July) Security-relevant: fixes approval responses being matched only by string ID, so an exec response could consume a patch waiter with the same ID. Hardens the approval boundary.

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #61844 — Intelligent Model Routing and Automatic Task Complexity Assessment — Proposes lightweight complexity assessment to auto-select model/reasoning level instead of manual switching.
  • #62213 — Built-in One-Click Prompt Enhancement for ChatGPT and Codex — Requests native "Optimize Prompt" in the input box, citing WorkBuddy/Kilo Code parity.

Q&A

  • #61849 — Diagnosing screenshot/tool response-start latency in Codex 0.169.0 — Asks for a supported metadata-only timing method to separate first-output latency from later command delivery.
  • #62436 — Supported architecture for continuing project ownership across runs — Building a NATS/JetStream-coordinated multi-worker system with durable project records; seeks official guidance.

Show and tell

  • #16329 — Awesome Codex CLI: 150+ ecosystem tools — Curated index of subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers.
  • #16073 — Awesome Codex Plugins community list — 12 official + 15 community plugins, manifest-verified.

  2. #21968 — Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents enough P2 · 7 comments Anecdotal but widely relatable: the model rarely invokes custom skills/subagents autonomously, even when highly relevant. Matters because it undermines the entire skills investment.

  3. #19873 — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing & post-execution intent routing P2 · 9 comments Maintainer-driven proposal to lean into Gemini 3's native bash affinity while keeping execution safe. The highest-comment issue in the batch and a strategic direction-setter.

  4. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland P1 · 4 comments Browser agent terminates with GOAL termination reason on Wayland sessions. Linux desktop users remain blocked; needs retesting.

  5. #22186 — get-shit-done output hook causes crash P1 · 3 comments Crash occurs during the final user-summary print of a hook. Reproducible-sounding and quota-wasting.

  6. #20079 — Symlinked agent files not recognized P2 · 4 comments ~/.gemini/agents/*.md symlinks fail agent discovery. A small but sharp DX papercut for dotfile-managed setups.

  7. #21763 — Bug reports omit subagent context P1 · 2 comments /bug output only captures the main session, making subagent failures effectively undiagnosable. Compounds the pain of every other agent bug.

  8. #17758 — Subagent resumability & persistence P2 · 3 comments · 👍 1 Epic tracking cross-session subagent resumption. Foundational for long-running agent workflows.

  9. #17754 — Async & background subagent execution P2 · 2 comments Enables non-blocking subagent runs — a prerequisite for parallel agent collaboration (#18287).

  10. #18062 — Cloud Shell API error "Requested entity was not found" P2 · 2 comments Lab Account users hit API failures inside an environment where the CLI is actively promoted. Adoption-blocking for education/enterprise onboarding.

  1. #30157 — Only replace true cycles with [Circular] in safeJsonStringify CLOSED · P2 Fixes false-positive cycle detection that corrupted telemetry, since OTel shares arrays (endTime, boundaries) across data points.

  2. #30156 — Buffer chat compression events until OTel SDK ready CLOSED · P2 logChatCompression was the lone logger bypassing bufferTelemetryEvent, causing dropped events on early init.

  3. #30334 — Parse PowerShell commands asynchronously to prevent UI freeze CLOSED · P2 · size/xl Eliminates multi-second spinner freezes on Windows during PowerShell AST validation. Large but high-impact UX fix.

  4. #30376 — Expand Windows home-relative paths using tilde and backslash OPEN Fixes ~\... resolution on Windows, which previously broke policy paths, extension registries, and include dirs.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in the source dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from the issue set, the dominant directions are:

  • Subagent maturity (the overwhelming theme): async/background execution (#17754), resumability & persistence (#17758), per-agent configurability of tools/policy/hooks/skills (#17760), non-blocking tool confirmations (#17756), UI/UX polish (#17761), and shared memory / parallel collaboration (#18287).
  • Native-bash-native agent design: sandboxing plus post-execution intent routing to exploit Gemini 3's POSIX-tool affinity (#19873).
  • Token-frugal context management: "Tactful Extraction" surgical read hierarchy (grep-first) to combat context bloat (#19561).
  • Persistent, file-based task tracking: replacing in-context WriteToDo with CRUD-backed tracking to survive context rot and session boundaries (#18836, #21000).
  • Agent self-awareness: accurate knowledge of its own flags, hotkeys, and self-execution (#21432).
  • Remote agent auth: OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration for A2A agents (#17604).
  • Per-workspace policy scoping instead of global-only policy (#18397).
  • Better agent examples in-repo to seed the subagent ecosystem (#18283).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Subagent reliability and observability. The cluster of P1 bugs — generalist agent hangs (#21409), browser agent Wayland failures (#21983), crash-on-hook-output (#22186), codebase_investigator schema-validation loops consuming quota (#17648), and bug reports that omit subagent context (#21763) — means users frequently cannot tell why an agent failed or even reproduce the failure. Quota waste during silent failure loops is a recurring complaint.
  • Under-triggering of skills/subagents. Even when correctly configured, the model frequently ignores skills and subagents unless explicitly instructed (#21968), making the configurability investment feel unrewarded.
  • Windows and Linux desktop papercuts. PowerShell parsing freezes (#30334), ~\ path resolution (#30376), and Wayland browser failures (#21983) form a persistent cross-platform tax.
  • Discovery/configuration friction. Symlinked agent files aren't recognized (#20079), and there's no settings.json-based subagent discovery yet (#18285).
  • Environment-specific onboarding blockers. Cloud Shell Lab Account API errors (#18062) hit users in an environment Google actively promotes, undercutting first-run success.
  • Context economics. Baseline context cost (~36.6k tokens/turn) and large file-read bloat drive repeated calls for surgical read strategies (#19561) and persistent out-of-context task state (#18836).

Result: no auth, no error, no popup. High engagement (8 comments, 👍3) reflects broad frustration with opaque MCP auth failures.

  2. #4203 [OPEN] — Expired MCP access token forces interactive re-auth instead of using the cached refresh token per RFC 6749 §6. Highly upvoted (👍5) — directly impacts unattended/automation workflows.

  3. #1168 [OPEN] — "Authorization fatigue": a single high-level request generated more than a dozen permission prompts. A long-running complaint (open since January) that keeps resurfacing.

  4. #5283 [OPEN, triage:needs-human] — Remote environment hosting blocked by remote-control policy on personal Copilot Free accounts. Highest upvote count in this batch (👍6), signaling a policy/entitlement gap.

  5. #5516 [OPEN] — store_memory offers scope: "user" even when user-level memory is unavailable; every user-scoped store fails with 404, and /memory off disables both scopes. New (filed 2026-11-19) but immediately relevant to memory-scope UX.

  6. #5517 [OPEN] — Pasted PDF counted at encoded file size (~620k estimated vs ~31k real tokens), triggering unnecessary compaction. A 20x overestimate that wastes context budget — companion to the known image-counting issue #2936.

  7. #4310 [OPEN] — Engine silently falls back to a hardcoded 128K token budget when a routed model reports no/zero capability limits, driving compaction incorrectly for 1M-token models.

  8. #5350 [CLOSED] — MCP OAuth interactive flow: authorization code received and success page served, but code→token exchange never runs — server stuck "Connecting". Closed, but symptomatic of the auth-state-machine fragility seen across #4017, #4769, #4371.

  9. #5510 [OPEN] — Linux/WSL: Entra MCP browser sign-in stalls silently when xdg-open is missing; /mcp Authenticate shows a URL that then fails with "State mismatch." Split out of #4017 by a maintainer.

Only one PR was updated in the last 24h:

  1. #2957 [CLOSED] — fix: extension bootstrap path mismatch in launchExtension() (#2890). Extensions failed to load on macOS and Windows because the forked child's security check expects the bootstrap path under dirname(process.execPath) (SEA binary dir), while app.js passed a path from the pkg cache (universal/<ver>/preloads/). Closes a cross-platform extension-loading blocker.

No other PRs were updated in the last 24 hours; the remaining recommended PR slots are empty for this window.

No Discussions data was provided for this window — section omitted.

  • Session forking & parallel workflows — #4580: /fork should open a new terminal, plus a copilot --fork startup flag.

  • MCP OAuth is the #1 reliability gap. A cluster of issues (#4017, #4203, #5350, #4769, #4371, #5510) describes silent failures, missing token exchange, redirect-metadata mismatch, unsupported URL elicitation for 3LO, and forced re-auth despite valid refresh tokens. Errors are frequently invisible — "no auth, no error, no popup" is a recurring phrase.
  • Permission/authorization fatigue (#1168, #5283): excessive prompts per request and policy blocks on personal/free accounts impede flow.
  • Context budget mismanagement (#5517, #4310, #4424): encoded-size counting for PDFs, silent 128K fallback, and /compact failing at the 5 MB CAPI limit can kill sessions outright.

  8. #12278 — [OPEN] Refresh scoped models on interactive reload — Makes /reload pick up enabledModels changes without restarting. Fixes #12277.
  9. #12319 — [OPEN] Make Codex system prompts cacheable — Moves the system prompt out of top-level instructions so it falls inside GPT-6.2's cacheable input prefix. Directly addresses the cache-reuse regression in #12273.
  10. #12325 — [OPEN] Keep GitHub Copilot's available models up to date — Refreshes availableModelIds on model refresh, not just token refresh. Fixes #11006.

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • #12331 — Pi-Personal: an always-on personal agent on pi — One pi session per agent kept alive in Herdr Core, reachable via Telegram, with plain-file message passing and ~5,216 lines of glue. A concrete example of using pi as an embedded agent runtime.

Ideas

  • #12320 — Reusing free chat quotas through a WebDriver — Speculative proposal to drive free chat web UIs via WebDriver as AI backends for editors. Explicitly noted as unrelated to Pi core, but generating interest.
  • #12314 — Rename codemode — Report that models (e.g., DeepSeek V4.1-Flash) frequently hallucinate codemod/codemodule instead of codemode, suggesting a more distinctive tool name.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Storage lifecycle management — #11026 (hard-delete conversations) and #12306 (hold restored work while admitting new requests) show users pushing pi-durable beyond simple persistence toward operational control.
  • Package/namespace composition — #8834 proposed an opt-in pi.namespace for skills and prompt templates, hinting at a desire for stronger namespacing as the extension ecosystem grows.
  • Editor/IDE integration via ACP — #10389 asked for an ACP adapter for Pi Durable, targeting JetBrains IDEs.
  • Cache-preserving session mutations — #12269 requests that changing thinking level mid-conversation not break the prompt cache on openai-codex.
  • Extension UI affordances — #12326 asks for a display-only gutter on sent user messages, indicating demand for finer-grained TUI customization.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows is a second-class citizen — The 99-comment #7547 thread plus #9549 (re-render saturation on 2-core Windows) and #12133 (mouse reports leaking after exit on Windows Terminal) show persistent friction across setup, performance, and terminal state on Windows.
  • Terminal state not restored on exit/suspend — A cluster of issues (#12133, #12272, #12338) and PRs (#12283, #12336, #12339) all trace to Pi leaving mouse tracking, Kitty keyboard protocol, or bracketed paste enabled. This is the single most concentrated bug theme today.
  • Prompt-cache regressions on new models — #12273 (GPT-6.2 vs 6.1 on Codex) and #12269 (thinking-level changes break caching) show caching is fragile across model/provider updates and directly affects token cost.
  • Enterprise/Copilot auth and model visibility — #12318 (Anthropic Team seat login fails) and #11006 (Copilot enterprise models hidden after restart) both hit corporate users specifically, pointing to stale credential/metadata handling.
  • Catalog drift — #12259 (missing qwen4-max/qwen4-max-preview in the Individual plan allowlist) and #12264 (OpenAI Decisions classifying cache usage as zero) suggest provider metadata is manually curated and easily falls behind upstream changes.
  • TUI input/selection correctness — #12245 (search picks wrong provider) and #12312 (Enter on an absolute-path Tab menu submits the prompt) reflect a class of small but annoying TUI interaction bugs that erode trust during daily use.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-20

1. Today's Highlights

CI reliability dominates the activity this cycle: the Managed Agent full tier has been chronically red on main since at least 2026-11-11 (#17851), while a security-sensitive trust bypass in AUTO mode (#17854) and a token-accounting bug that can kill a turn after auto-compaction (#15486) are the most consequential open bugs. On the feature side, work continues on managed-channel identity binding, MCP elicitation, and skill-level MCP dependency surfacing.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate, no test identified (484 comments). A bot-filed CI failure that has become the single most-commented issue in the repo. Its volume reflects repeated re-triggers rather than distinct problems, but it's a strong signal that the Managed Agent gate is unstable and noisy.

  2. #15486 — Compaction double-counts pending tool result, pads 20K, sends max_tokens: 1 (P1). A correctness bug in the token-management path with a clear repro: after auto-compaction mid-tool-loop, the next request's size estimate counts a pending tool result twice, aborting the turn. High impact for long agent sessions.

  3. #17854 — AUTO mode: server-level MCP trust bypasses the LLM classifier (P1, security). A structural design gap: tools added after a trusted MCP server was approved execute with zero review. This is the most important security thread right now since it undermines the AUTO-mode threat model.

  4. #17037 — hz3 /tmp out of inodes; leftover verify work trees hold 92% of tmpfs (P1). Runner infrastructure is failing jobs before they start. This is an ops-level blocker for contributors landing on the hz3 host.

  5. #17851 — Managed Agent full tier chronically red; Hosted failover E2E runtime_preparation_timeout (P1). Confirmed red on main independent of any PR since ≥2026-11-11, which means required-check gating is effectively meaningless for that scope.

  6. #17039 — Make the Managed Agent gate name stable so it can become a required check (P1). Directly tied to #17851's root cause: an unstable gate name let a PR merge with a red Java suite.

  7. #17832 — MCP server still connecting is reported as failed; late-arriving tools never reach the model. A user-visible correctness issue in the daemon/VS Code companion: a server that connects 20s later is labeled failed, and its tools never surface.

  8. #17188 — DeepSeek V3.1/V3.2 fall back to the generic output limit. Model-id normalization misses the bundled catalog's 65,536-token entries, silently capping output at 32K.

  9. #17628 — CLI command migration can overwrite a newly created Markdown file. A check-then-write race with data-loss potential, plus a dangling-symlink hole.

  10. #17859 — Web Shell: iOS Safari keyboard covers Send on welcome screen. A concrete mobile UX regression with a clean repro; representative of the growing set of Web Shell client polish issues.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17775 — Bind the GitHub ledger to its registration identity. Mirrors the WeCom/DingTalk adapter pattern, closing a cross-ownership pending-replay class of bugs in managed channels.

  2. #17894 — Keep what the person typed in a reduced compaction request. Fixes a real UX defect where user prompts were truncated to 4,000 chars during compaction-window reduction.

  3. #17875 — Protect persisted tool-output recovery. Extends microcompaction protection to producer-attached recovery metadata, complementing #17337's stub-detection work.

  4. #17323 — Surface unconfigured MCP dependencies at skill activation. Lets SKILL.md declare mcp: dependencies and reports missing ones with remediation at activation time — a nice usability win for skill authors.

  5. #17358 — Declare MCP elicitation capability + protocol-level decline handler. Protocol-completeness work that unblocks servers relying on elicitation/create.

  6. #17458 — Reject record_artifact on files inside skipped artifact directories. Closes a visibility gap where ignored files could reappear in the Artifacts panel.

  7. #17677 — Daemon restart recovery inbox. Adds POST /sessions/recovery endpoints so unsettled prompts can be listed and resumed after a daemon restart — meaningful durability for long-running sessions.

  8. #17864 / #17871 — Converge pre-production managed-agent version machinery. Removes rolling-upgrade compatibility scaffolding and advances the files-on-v2 lifecycle; large but well-scoped cleanup.

  9. #17890 — Deliver pending async hook output on the ACP legacy round. Closes the last model-round surface that silently dropped background hook output.

  10. #17533 — Web Shell worktree carry metadata + snapshot-then-delete cleanup. Advances Codex-parity for managed session worktrees, recording dirty overlays carried in from the source tree.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided for this cycle; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Session management & recovery: Daemon restart recovery (#17677), agent-loop follow-ups (#17284), and session-management roadmap work dominate feature-shaped activity.
  • Managed channel integrations: Repeated deferred follow-ups across DingTalk, GitHub, and WeCom adapters (#17769, #17813, #17775) indicate managed-agent card/channel breadth is the active expansion front.
  • MCP capability depth: Elicitation, skill-declared MCP dependencies, and trust-model refinements (#17358, #17323, #17854) are converging into a coherent MCP roadmap.
  • Permission/interaction protocol: #17715 asks for uninspectable permission subjects to be a first-class protocol state rather than a layout accident — a sign that interactive permission UX is maturing.
  • Configuration surfaces: #14507 (closed) asked for a supported way to enable LSP in the Desktop client without CLI flags — the recurring "expose experimental features via settings" theme.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Chronically red CI on main: Issues #17851, #17039, #14724, and #11680 all point to the same root frustration: failures merge past unstable gates, then every subsequent PR inherits them. The 484-comment CI issue is the clearest evidence of bot-noise fatigue.
  • Flaky tests generating issue churn: #17834, #17884, #17791, and #16531 show a steady stream of deflake work, often with the reviewer bot explicitly warning "if it fails again it's a real bug, do NOT stabilize."
  • Token/compaction correctness: #15486 and #17337 reflect a pattern of subtle accounting errors in the compaction path that are hard to reproduce but silently degrade long sessions.
  • Model-catalog normalization gaps: #17188 and #17189 reveal that model-id parsing drops vendor prefixes and vision flags, quietly misconfiguring limits and inputs for third-party models.
  • MCP lifecycle ambiguity: #17832 captures a recurring class of confusion where "still connecting" is indistinguishable from "failed" to the user.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-20

Issues: 466 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-20 02:14 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-20

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity but upgrade-fragile state. Activity is intense: 466 issues and 500 PRs touched in the last 24h, with roughly 72% of issues still open and 61% of PRs awaiting review — a large but manageable intake funnel. Two releases landed (v2026.11.6 stable and v2026.11.10-beta.1), headlined by agent templates from ClawHub and OpenClaw ID node connectivity, alongside upgrade-path hardening. However, the issue tracker is dominated by update/Doctor failures, state-DB corruption, prompt-cache invalidation, and session persistence bugs, several tagged P0/P1 as release blockers. Overall health: strong feature momentum, strained release-engineering reliability — the update pipeline is the single biggest source of user pain.

2. Releases

v2026.11.10-beta.1 (beta)

  • Agent templates: add agents directly from ClawHub packages via a single CLAW.md manifest with bundled skill folders validated by the native trust flow (#195707, #196322, #196348) — authored by @steipete, thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
  • OpenClaw ID: node connection work begins (release notes truncated in source data).
  • Migration notes: Template-based agent installation is new; no breaking changes stated in the visible notes. As a beta, expect the known update-path issues below to apply.

v2026.11.6 (stable)

  • Smoother upgrades: bridges the 2026.11.5 updater to the current release path and correctly validates staged plugin dependencies on Windows (#200662, #200595) — authored by @steipete, thanks @RomneyDa and @desksk.
  • More resilient conversations: subagent/session handling improvements (notes truncated).
  • Breaking changes: none stated. This is a targeted reliability release responding to the update failures reported across #200606, #199617, and #200289.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed activity today (193 PRs closed or merged) skews toward template UX, gateway correctness, and diagnostics:

  • Template/ClawHub UX maturation: #202060 (preview a Template without expanding files), #202126 (show planned automations with controls in chat), #202115 (correct agent/activity display when adding a template), #202156 (idle worker heap collection), #202168 (Crabbox wrapper test fix).
  • Gateway fixes: #199743 (refresh native command channels when the plugin registry is replaced — fixes Telegram slash commands breaking after hot reload), #202166 (preserve transport identity on oversized history placeholders).
  • Upgrade diagnostics: #202174 (keep Doctor finding targets in upgrade failure reports) and #199651 (distinguish invalid Windows Scheduled Task inspection responses) — both directly aimed at the opaque update failures dominating the tracker.
  • iOS transcript rebuild: #200592 closed after reworking the iOS chat around the web reading model (pagination, grouped tool calls, turn summaries).

Directionally, the team is converting update-failure reports into diagnostic improvements rather than only point fixes — a healthy sign, but the underlying state-migration machinery remains fragile.

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL verification leaves 11.3 update partially finalized (P0) 29 Update integrity; state-migrated-no-rollback trap
2 #119720 — Synchronous agent persistence blocks Gateway event loop at scale (P1) 29, 👍2 Scalability of the core session store
3 #123792 — Assistant turns render twice with CLI backends (P2) 20 Transcript duplication across surfaces
4 #125764 — Telegram outbound sends dead-lettered after one attempt (P1) 15, 👍1 Silent message loss in adapters
5 #200606 — Candidate Doctor blocks 11.3→11.5 with migration conflict (P1) 14, 👍1 Same update cluster

Underlying needs: the community is converging on two themes — (a) update/migration transactions must be atomic and recoverable, and (b) message delivery must never silently drop. The persistence/event-loop and Telegram dead-letter threads are months old with diamond/platinum-lobster ratings, indicating deep, well-evidenced problems rather than noise.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / release blockers

  • #197083 — Doctor WAL publication verification fails mid-update; leaves partially finalized installs. No fix PR linked. ⚠️
  • #164800 — Managed update stalls after Doctor with Gateway stopped (9.7→9.8), still unresolved since October. No fix PR.
  • #158277 — Talk on Apple Watch fails with "Voice changed its remote network address" (P0, release blocker). Fix-shape clear, no PR yet.

P1

  • #119720 — Gateway event-loop blocking from synchronous persistence at scale.
  • #125764 — Telegram single-attempt dead-lettering (message loss).
  • #198218 — Doctor/update maintenance livelock re-hashing unchanged state DB.
  • #196199 — Codex helper completions fail to resume parent (regression since 2026.10.10).
  • #194655 — Deferred plugin DB migration ends in state-migrated-no-rollback (workboard schema 38 vs 0).
  • #169797 — Gateway memory regression (~2.5x) on single-CPU hosts.
  • #191476 — Matrix room stuck on "consumer is closed" after image_generate race.

P2 highlights

  • #191847 — 512 MB SQLite worker OOM kills large sessions (regression since 2026.10.10).
  • #198373 & #202001 — Prompt-cache invalidation: history rewritten / system-prompt section churn collapses cache reads to ~1–3% on OpenAI-compatible routes. This is an emerging cluster worth watching; PR #201710 ("freeze a prompt series' tool set at its first request") is an open candidate fix.
  • #112638 — Session maintenance limits silently exceeded (thread/channel entries exempt from reclaim).
  • #170496 — Full state-DB copy per read; cron tick triggers it repeatedly.

Positive signal: closed today — #200289 (11.3→11.4 SQLite-lock update failure), #199155 (CLI message send transcript race), #201796 (cron replay loop), #164355 (plugin hook gap). Several had clear fix shapes and were queueable — maintainer throughput is working.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Memory search / CJK: #170997 requests a bigram tokenizer (trigram yields 0 matches for 2-char Chinese queries). #179954 asks for configurable per-entry chunking paths — both are low-risk, high-value and plausible for an upcoming beta.
  • Cron lifecycle: #130247 — no --until/--max-runs; jobs cannot self-terminate.
  • Channel scheduling: #187264 — caller-scoped, same-conversation scheduling for non-owner Slack users (needs product + security review).
  • Automation UX: #150029 (closed) — configurable Inspect link (always | errors | never).
  • In-flight: PR #202171 adds realtime voice token accounting (Discord/Talk/Voice Call) — closes #202165. PR #159478 adds selective agent participation in group conversations.

Prediction: given the template/ClawHub push in v2026.11.10-beta.1, expect template automation controls, voice cost accounting, and memory-search tokenizer work to land next; cron lifecycle and group-conversation features are more likely post-stabilization.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (ranked by recurrence):

  1. Updates break or stall — the dominant theme. Users report multi-hour updates, SQLite locks during Gateway handoff requiring SSH recovery (#200289), Doctor blocking valid migrations (#200606), Windows Scheduled Task validation failures (#199617), and state-migrated-no-rollback dead ends (#197083, #194655). Trust in the updater is the top satisfaction risk.
  2. Silent message loss — Telegram dead-lettering (#125764) and Matrix consumer-closed races (#191476) drop high-value messages with no user-visible error.
  3. Performance/cost — prompt-cache collapse (#198373, #202001) directly increases token spend; memory regression on small hosts (#169797) and worker OOM (#191847) hit low-resource users hardest.
  4. Session state integrity — duplicate renders (#123792), phantom replies from stale injected context (#177210), and unbounded session stores (#112638).

Satisfaction signals: high-quality, well-reproduced reports (diamond/platinum-lobster ratings) suggest an engaged, technically sophisticated community; rapid closure of several P1s today indicates responsiveness once issues are triaged.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or high-impact items needing maintainer attention:

Item Age Why it matters
#119720 (P1, since Aug) ~3.5 mo Gateway event-loop blocking — architectural; affects all large deployments
#112638 (P2, since Jul) ~4 mo Session store limits silently exceeded; needs product decision
#125764 (P1, since Aug) ~3 mo Telegram message loss; no fix PR, needs live repro
#164800 (P0, since Oct) ~1.5 mo Update stall, unresolved — undermines the entire release channel
#130247 (P3, since Aug) ~3 mo Cron jobs cannot end; stale, needs product decision
#153899 (P1, since Sep) ~2 mo Gateway drain waits full TimeoutStopSec; stale + needs info
PR #129388 (since Aug) ~3 mo Context-pressure-aware continuation — XL design PR stuck needing proof/security review
PR #192350 (since Nov 3) ~2.5 wk GitHub integration → plugin migration; security review required

Recommendation: the update/Doctor failure cluster (#197083, #164800, #200606, #198218, #194655) should be treated as a single coordinated release-engineering epic — it is the highest-leverage fix for user trust, and v2026.11.6's targeted hardening suggests the team already recognizes this.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw — issues/PRs updated 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-20. Comment counts and 👍 as reported in the snapshot; "undefined" comment counts on PRs reflect missing data in the source feed.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report: Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot Date: 2026-11-20

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant open-source landscape on 2026-11-20 is characterized by intense feature velocity paired with release-engineering fragility. All four active projects (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw) show elevated issue/PR throughput, but only Hermes Agent shipped a stable release (v0.23.3) in the window; OpenClaw's beta landed atop a persistent update-failure cluster, QwenPaw sits in a regression-heavy post1 stabilization phase, and ZeroClaw recorded zero merges in 24h ahead of its v0.9.1 gate. A common maturation arc is visible: every project is simultaneously modularizing (plugin/MCP extraction), hardening update/migration paths, and pushing channel-adapter parity. IronClaw was inactive.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (updated/24h) PRs (updated/24h) Merged/Closed PRs Release Status Health Score*
OpenClaw 466 (~72% open) 500 (~61% awaiting review) 193 v2026.11.6 stable + v2026.11.10-beta.1 6.5 / 10 (feature-strong, update-fragile)
Hermes Agent 50 50 8 v0.23.3 stable (~370 PR rollup) + canary 7.0 / 10 (strong throughput, P2 backlog)
QwenPaw 24 32 (25 open / 7 closed) 7 No release today; v2.3.0.post1 regression phase 6.0 / 10 (responsive but regression-heavy)
ZeroClaw 12 (10 open / 2 closed) 50 (all open) 0 None; v0.9.1 gate crunch 5.0 / 10 (merge-queue pileup, S1 hang)
IronClaw — — — — Dormant

*Health scores are subjective composites of throughput, merge velocity, open high-severity bugs, and release cadence — intended for relative ranking, not absolute comparison.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Order-of-magnitude larger surface area — ~10x the issue/PR volume of Hermes or QwenPaw; ~930 items touched in 24h vs. 100 for Hermes.
  • Fastest response on triage — 193 PRs closed/merged in 24h, the highest absolute throughput in the cohort.
  • Most complete channel matrix already shipped (Telegram, Matrix, Slack, Discord, Voice Call, Talk, Apple Watch) — Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw are still closing channel-parity gaps (Hermes: BlueBubbles, Slack; QwenPaw: QQ, WeChat, DingTalk/Feishu; ZeroClaw: XMPP, Discord/Matrix approval buttons).
  • Template/ClawHub distribution model (v2026.11.10-beta.1) — a first-class agent packaging/manifest ecosystem (CLAW.md + bundled skill folders) that no peer currently matches.

Technical approach differences:

  • Gateway-centric architecture with a shared SQLite state DB and WAL-based migration pipeline — powerful but the direct source of its update fragility.
  • Session persistence is synchronous and blocks the event loop at scale (#119720), an architectural debt peers have partially avoided by isolating gateways.
  • Prompt-cache series freezing (PR #201710) is a leading indicator OpenClaw is optimizing for token economics on OpenAI-compatible routes — Hermes and QwenPaw are earlier in this cycle.

Community size comparison: OpenClaw's engagement profile (diamond/platinum-lobster-rated issues, 29-comment threads, multiple P0s under sustained discussion) indicates a technically sophisticated, high-trust user base an order of magnitude larger than the others. Hermes reports low 👍 counts (functional engagement); QwenPaw's users invest in detailed repros but are fewer; ZeroClaw's RFC culture is high-quality but small (CastelloBrancoTecnologia, NiuBlibing are repeatedly named contributors).

Net position: OpenClaw is the reference platform — feature-complete and widely deployed — but its update/Doctor reliability is the ecosystem's single biggest trust risk. A coordinated release-engineering epic (#197083, #164800, #200606, #198218, #194655) would convert its size advantage into a decisive lead.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirements surfacing across two or more projects:

Theme OpenClaw Hermes QwenPaw ZeroClaw Underlying Need
Update/migration atomicity #197083, #164800, #200606, #194655 (implicit via v0.23.3 rollup) post1 regressions #8811/#8812/#8815 v0.9.1 gate (#11580, #12476) Recoverable, transactional upgrades — no state-migrated-no-rollback dead ends
Silent failure elimination #125764 (Telegram), #191476 (Matrix) #158043 (notif truncation), #156923 (Slack loop) #8475 (QQ flag reset), #8313, #8814 (WeChat) #12569 (plugin false-load) Failures must surface logs/warnings rather than drop messages or channels
Plugin/MCP modularization ClawHub templates, trust flow ACP session config (#81067), desktop MCP (#158065) #8469 (MCP plugin), #8499 (local models) #12216 (multi-registry origins) Clean plugin boundaries with validated manifests
Provider/credential correctness Codex helper regression (#196199) #158061, #117442 (classifier) #8579 → #8825 (disabled provider) #11296 (URI ignored), #12422 (scoped creds RFC) Predictable routing and never exposing credentials to the model
Cost/budget transparency Prompt-cache invalidation (#198373, #202001) — Prefix-cache instability (#6952) #10635 (global vs. profile budget), #12568 Operators need accurate, non-misleading spend controls
Local/offline model support — #153962 (Ollama tool-call corruption) #8826 (Rapid-MLX), #8472 (reranker) #11296 (llama.cpp URI) Privacy-first deployments must work end-to-end
Channel approval parity mature across channels Mobile capabilities (#142277) #8827 (Telegram forum isolation) #12557 (Discord/Matrix emoji) Consistent UX for human-in-the-loop approval
Session/transcript integrity #123792 (dup renders), #112638 #154326 (stale anchor) #8811 (UI containment) #11676 (created_at corruption) Deterministic, paginated transcripts

Convergent insight: Every project is fighting the same three battles — updates that cannot corrupt state, channels that cannot silently die, and costs that cannot surprise users. These are now table-stakes requirements for any serious personal-agent deployment.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Axis OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Primary focus Agent template ecosystem + broadest channel matrix Desktop/mobile + multi-profile enterprise routing China-region channels (QQ/WeChat/DingTalk/Feishu) + memory/retrieval Rust performance + security/credential scoping
Target users Power users, self-hosters, template authors Teams, multi-profile operators, desktop-centric users Regional (CN) deployments, WeChat/QQ integrators Security-conscious ops, edge/self-hosted infra teams
Architecture Gateway + shared SQLite + WAL migrations Gateway + desktop client + profile-scoped state Channel-isolated workers + plugin extraction arc Rust daemon + canonical provider registry (V5)
Distribution ClawHub + CLAW.md manifests GitHub / Microsoft Store / Docker / Hermes Cloud Website docs + multi-channel installers Release binaries with 64 MiB size gate
Language / stack TypeScript/Node + native SQLite Mixed (TS + desktop) Python (AgentScope lineage) Rust
Security model Native trust flow for templates Provider-safety refusal classification tool_guard (with #8513 AUTO/SMART gap closed) RFC #12422 scoped operator credentials (V5 stack)
Momentum stage Scaling a mature platform Stabilizing after large rollup Post-regression stabilization Pre-release merge crunch

Strategic read:

  • OpenClaw is the horizontal platform play — widest surface, richest ecosystem, but bounded by release reliability.
  • Hermes is the workflow/desktop play — its multi-profile friction (#112627, #146035, #151990, #154627, #157976) is the roadmap signal; solving config inheritance unlocks its enterprise story.
  • QwenPaw is the regional + memory play — its Channel + memory investment (#8472 reranker, #7019 memory search separation) pairs with CN channel dominance; its blunt UI/UX feedback (#8817 "disaster-level") is a corrective signal.
  • ZeroClaw is the security/performance play — the only Rust-first project, driving a credential-scoping RFC and canonical provider registry that others will likely adopt conceptually.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tiers by activity and maturity:

Tier Projects Characteristics
Tier 1 — Scaling platform OpenClaw ~930 items/24h, 193 merged, largest community; strained by release engineering, not adoption
Tier 2 — High-velocity stabilizer Hermes Agent 50/50 issues/PRs, 8 merges, stable release shipped; P2 backlog aging 3–6 months
Tier 3 — Regression recovery QwenPaw 24/32, 7 merged; same-day regression fixes are a strength, but 5 regressions from one release window is a warning
Tier 4 — Release-gate crunch ZeroClaw 50 open PRs, 0 merges — highest pileup risk; strong RFC culture but lowest short-term throughput
Inactive IronClaw No activity

Rapidly iterating: OpenClaw (feature releases, template ecosystem), Hermes (370-PR rollup cadence). Stabilizing: QwenPaw (fixing post1 regressions), ZeroClaw (v0.9.1 gate but with merge paralysis).

Merge-queue health ranking: OpenClaw > Hermes > QwenPaw > ZeroClaw. ZeroClaw's zero-merge day is the outlier; a sustained 50-PR backlog with dependent stacks (#12450→#12452→#12453) is a contributor-fatigue risk.

7. Trend Signals

Extracted for AI agent developers:

  1. "Atomic updates or nothing" is now a competitive requirement. Across OpenClaw (#197083), QwenPaw (post1 regressions), and ZeroClaw (v0.9.1 gate), upgrade/state-migration integrity is the #1 trust-killer — not feature gaps. Invest in transactional state stores with rollback from day one.

  2. Silent failures are the new P0. Message loss and channel death (OpenClaw Telegram #125764, QwenPaw #8475/#8814, ZeroClaw #12569, Hermes #158043) recur universally. Design for observable failure — every dropped message/closed channel must emit a log and a user-visible signal.

  3. Prompt/cache economics are becoming architectural. OpenClaw's prompt-cache invalidation cluster (#198373, #202001, PR #201710) and QwenPaw's 3-month-old prefix-cache instability (#6952) show token economics are now a core runtime concern, not a tuning exercise. Preserve prompt series and tool-set stability by design.

  4. Local/offline model support is table stakes and currently under-delivered. Hermes #153962 (Ollama corruption) explicitly "completely blocks agentic use"; ZeroClaw #11296; QwenPaw #8826. Tool-call formatting over local backends is a persistent weak link — validate against Ollama, llama.cpp, and MLX early.

  5. Plugin/MCP standardization is the 2027 battleground. Every project is extracting plugins (OpenClaw ClawHub templates, Hermes ACP + MCP, QwenPaw #8469/#8499, ZeroClaw #12216). Manifest validation, trust flows, and multi-registry origins will define ecosystem lock-in.

  6. Credential scoping is a maturing security theme. ZeroClaw's RFC #12422 ("authorize the action, never expose the credential to the model") is the clearest articulation; OpenClaw's template trust flow and QwenPaw's closed tool_guard gap (#8513) point the same direction. Treat credentials as operator-managed, action-scoped resources.

  7. Cost transparency is a trust primitive, not a dashboard nicety. ZeroClaw #10635 (global vs. profile budget mismatch) and #12568 (always-full cost bars) show misleading cost UX erodes operator trust as fast as a crash.

  8. Config inheritance and multi-profile hygiene are unmet in mature projects. Hermes' systemic profile friction (#112627 and five related open issues) is the strongest roadmap signal in the cohort — the winner will be whoever ships clean profile-scoped config/state resolution first.

Bottom line for developers: Build for recoverable state, observable failure, cache-stable prompts, and scoped credentials — these are the four patterns that separate the projects users trust from those they merely use. Platform breadth (OpenClaw's play) and vertical depth (ZeroClaw's security or QwenPaw's regional channels) are both viable, but neither survives an unreliable upgrade path.

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest

1. Today's Overview

Hermes Agent shows very high activity on 2026-11-20: 50 issues and 50 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, with a new patch release (v0.23.3) rolling up ~370 merged PRs since v0.23.2. The project is clearly in a stabilization phase for the v0.23.x line, with v0.24.0 curated notes expected to follow. Activity is dominated by bug fixes across gateway, desktop, agent runtime, and provider integrations — a healthy sign of active maintenance, though the backlog of long-lived P2 bugs (some dating to May 2026) suggests maintainer triage bandwidth is a bottleneck. Overall project health is strong but strained: high throughput on PRs, but a growing pile of unresolved core issues.

Assessment: No breaking changes to announce this cycle. The large PR rollup (370 PRs) indicates aggressive merge velocity and a healthy contribution pipeline.

3. Project Progress

PRs merged/closed in last 24h: 8. Notable closed PRs advancing fixes:

  • #134830 [CLOSED] — fix(kanban): separate worker liveness from progress; bound runtime by estimate. Decouples heartbeat liveness from forward progress, giving the kanban dispatcher an enforceable runtime budget. Fixes a class of "phantom active workers" bugs.
  • #146651 [CLOSED] — fix(tui_gateway): cap pdf.attach page render size. Replaces fixed-DPI full-size PNG rendering with long-edge-capped JPEG; adds raster and embedded-image fallbacks. Closes #146639.
  • #118681 [CLOSED] — fix(tests): align Windows fleet fallback with identity contract. Test infrastructure alignment for Windows control-socket fallback.

Feature advancement (open PRs in flight):

  • Desktop in-app offers — #158060 adds signed Portal offer dialogs, shown once as a dismissible dialog.
  • Mobile device capability requests — #142277 enables agents to access phone camera/GPS/screen over the gateway.
  • A2A accept-then-poll workflow — #141947 adds bounded client polling and task-ID resume.
  • Structured memory prefetch observations — #92118 adds an optional provider-neutral side channel.

4. Community Hot Topics

Most active Issues:

    • Tagged blocked, cause/upstream. Fork-based PR creation fails for a specific contributor account; issue creation and fork PRs still work.

The project is in a post-v2.3.0.post1 stabilization phase: at least five regressions (#8811, #8812, #8815, #8796, #8814) trace directly to the v2.3.0/post1 upgrade window, and several have already attracted candidate fix PRs (#8823, #8824, #8825). Overall project health is active but strained: responsiveness to individual reports is good (same-day fixes appearing), yet recurring architectural gaps (channel event handling, provider/model config coupling, storage lifecycle) keep generating duplicate classes of bugs.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-20

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows very high PR throughput but a stalled merge pipeline: 50 PRs were updated in the last 24h, yet zero were merged or closed, leaving all 50 open. Issue activity is more balanced — 12 issues updated, 10 open and 2 closed — but several are high-risk security/runtime items (risk:high) that remain unresolved. Notably, the project is in a release-gate crunch for v0.9.1, with two release-tagged issues (#11580 binary size cap, #12476 gateway log flooding) in play and no new releases published today. The most concerning signal is a new S1 (workflow-blocking) daemon startup hang (#12570) filed today, plus a cluster of credential/security RFC work (#12422 and dependent PRs) signaling the project is mid-refactor on its identity/access model. Overall health: active and ambitious, but merge velocity and release readiness are the bottlenecks.

2. Releases

None. No new releases published on 2026-11-20. The project is tracking toward v0.9.1, with at least two release-gated issues (#11580, #12476) and multiple PRs labeled release:v0.9.1 still open. No changelog, breaking changes, or migration notes to report.

Merged/closed PRs today: 0. No PRs landed in the last 24h — the entire 50-PR update set remains open. Progress is therefore visible only in issue closures:

  • #12217 [CLOSED] — Docs fix: Email tools-only setup now clarifies that approval routes also start the IMAP listener. (link)

  • Canonical provider registry (V5) — PRs #12450, #12452, #12453 form a dependent stack adopting a canonical model registry across providers, Zerocode, and the web UI.
  • Scoped credentials / identity-access — PRs #12408, #12490, #12596, #12438 implement operator-managed HTTP/browser/SSH credentials tied to RFC #12422.
  • Channels & plugins — XMPP channel (#11847), multi-registry plugin origins (#12216), and bounded tool-result preservation (#11911).

4. Community Hot Topics

Most-discussed items by comment count:

Item Comments Link

#12422 — RFC: Scoped use of operator-managed service credentials 3 issue

Underlying needs analysis:

  • #11296 reflects a real configuration-trust gap: users routing through non-localhost model routers (e.g., llama.cpp behind a proxy) find the configured URI silently ignored. This is core provider plumbing and blocks self-hosted/edge deployments.
  • #9345 is a maintainer-scale pain point — manual PR triage doesn't scale with 50-PR/day volume; automation is needed to keep risk labels honest.
  • #10635 exposes a cost-safety inconsistency: profiles advertise effectively unbounded budgets while a hardcoded $10/day global ledger rejects turns. This undermines operator trust in budget controls.
  • #12422 (RFC) is the anchor for a broad security refactor — the community is clearly pushing for "authorize the action, never expose the credential to the model."

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (newly reported/updated today):

🔴 S1 — Workflow blocked

  • #12570 — Daemon hangs at startup when the log directory holds millions of leaked runtime-trace.tmp.* files from failed rolling trims. Two compounding defects: temp-file leak on trim error + unbounded accumulation → startup hang. No fix PR identified. (link) — Highest priority; recommend immediate triage.

🟠 S2 — Degraded behavior

  • #12569 — plugin install / plugin list --verify falsely report a tool plugin as loading when a built-in tool name (e.g., weather) reserves it; runtime silently refuses registration. (link) — No fix PR.
  • #10635 — Cost-limit mismatch (see Hot Topics). status:in-progress, risk:high. (link)

🟡 S3 — Minor

  • #11296 — Provider URI ignored for llama.cpp/custom providers. status:accepted, risk:high. (link)
  • #12568 — Dashboard Cost Overview bars scale to the largest figure, so the Monthly bar is always full (cosmetic but misleading). (link)

✅ Closed today: #12476 (gateway INFO log flooding).

Fix-PR status: No open PR in this dataset is explicitly linked as a fix for #12570 or #12569 — these are unowned stability risks entering the release window.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Signal Likely next-version?

#11580 — Resolve binary size gate policy Release-blocking decision Must be decided for v0.9.1

Prediction: v0.9.1 will be dominated by release-gate and stability fixes (#11580, #12476, cost-limit #10635), not new features. The credential-scoping RFC (#12422) and its PR stack are the flagship v0.10 theme. Channel approval parity (#12557) and plugin multi-registry (#12216) are plausible fast-follows.

  • Self-hosted routing is fragile — users configuring llama.cpp/custom routers find their URI ignored (#11296); configuration trust is broken.
  • Budget controls are inconsistent — profiles claim unbounded cost, global ledger rejects at $10 (#10635). Operators cannot predict spend behavior.

  • Channel UX is uneven — Telegram has rich tool-approval buttons; Discord/Matrix lag behind (#12557).

Satisfaction/positive signals:

  • Active, high-quality RFC culture (#12422) with contributors (CastelloBrancoTecnologia, NiuBlibing) shipping large dependent PR stacks — indicates a committed, capable contributor base.
  • Rapid bug acknowledgment: #12476 closed within ~4 days; new bugs (#12569, #12570) filed with precise root-cause analysis (file:line references), suggesting sophisticated users.

Net: Users are technically advanced and demanding; the friction is concentrated in config correctness, cost transparency, and release reliability rather than core capability.

Recommend the maintainers prioritize (a) unblocking the S1 daemon hang, (b) resolving the #11580 release-size decision, and (c) triaging the oldest needs-author-action XL PRs to prevent contributor fatigue.
